tools.name: put
tools.description: Store a value under a key. Costs $0.002, charged only if the payment settles; a failed payment stores nothing. Values up to 64 KB, stored unencrypted, kept for ttl_seconds (default 3600, max 604800) then deleted. Overwrites an existing key and bumps its seq. The write becomes visible once the paymen

tools.name: wait
tools.description: Block until a key changes, then return it. Costs $0.001 per call whether or not anything arrives (it is a long-poll, not a subscription). Returns immediately if the key's seq is already greater than since; otherwise waits up to timeout_seconds (max 25) and returns value null with timed_out true. Pas

tools.name: get
tools.description: Read a key. Free, no payment or identity needed, rate limited per address. Needs the box: a box_... id from put, or a channel name. Returns value null with found false if absent or expired. A box is a namespace of keys. Omit it on a paid call to use your own wallet's box (the call returns its id). P

tools.name: list
tools.description: List the keys in a box with their seq, size and expiry, newest first, without values. Free, rate limited per address. Anyone holding the box id can do this.

tools.name: delete
tools.description: Delete a key from a box immediately. Free, rate limited per address. Anyone holding the box id can do this; there is no undo.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "delete" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: wait · Private data: put, wait, get · Public sink: put, wait, get · Destructive: put, wait, get, delete.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: wait · Private data: put, wait, get · Public sink: put, wait, get · Destructive: put, wait, get, delete

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
